# civgrad — historical replay scorecard

<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by `python3 -m validation.runner` — do not edit by hand. -->

Misses are displayed as prominently as hits: a model whose public scorecard
shows its misses is the product (PLAN.md §3). Nothing here is tuned to an
event; per-event inputs are documented facts from `validation/events/*.yaml`.

**Protocols.** `v0 imposed-τ`: capacity loss with an imposed exponential recovery
at the event's documented ramp τ; observes fab flow. `v1 adaptive`: capacity loss
is a pure impulse; recovery is emergent from the frozen adaptation law
(ALPHA=0.06, HORIZON=6 mo); observes the event's own observable (fab or
delivered). *dip* = deepest drop of the observed flow vs its pre-shock mean
(negative dip: the flow never fell — it rose). *recovery* = months from shock
until the flow re-crosses 95% of pre-shock; with a dip inside 5% the metric
degenerates to time-of-minimum.

## The documented miss: Sumitomo 1993 — xfail, twice

The model misses this event twice, in opposite directions. Protocol v0 (imposed-tau, observing fab flow) shows dip ~0%: packaging halts do not stop fabs, so through the fab observable the event is invisible — the wrong-observable failure from the design history. Protocol v1 (adaptive, observing delivered flow) shows a ~58% dip with no recovery inside the 72-month horizon — a hysteresis trap: the adaptation law rebuilds capacity, but the price-mediated demand reallocation that pulled the real system back in months does not exist in the model. This is the failing test that motivates the demand/allocation RFC (PLAN.md §6.4) and opened the packaging_resin oracle (map/_oracles/packaging_resin.yaml).

## Out of scope

- **2020-21 chip crunch (demand-side)** — demand surge + ordering whiplash while fab capacity stayed intact; shortages persisted ~2 years. Out of scope: no demand dynamics; see the demand/allocation RFC (PLAN.md §6.4).

## Counterfactuals (informational, never scored)

| replay | protocol | model dip | model recovery | note |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 2022 neon shock, WITHOUT stockpile | v0 imposed-τ | 24.1% | 12.8 mo | the 2014 lesson: what lean inventories would have cost |
| 2022 neon shock, WITHOUT stockpile | v1 adaptive | 17.5% | 6.7 mo | same counterfactual, under the adaptation law |
| 2019 photoresist (analog), feared (90%) | v1 adaptive | 64.0% | 13.7 mo | what the fear implied, had the curbs bitten fully |

**Pessimism-bias caveat.** The model has no price-mediated demand allocation,
substitution, or design-around response, so it systematically overstates how
bad supply shocks get and how long they last (Sumitomo v1 is the exhibit).
Rankings of *where* fragility concentrates are more trustworthy than absolute
dip depths. See METHODOLOGY.md §5-6.
